I'm not even going into the problems with the servers, which are thankfully a lot better nowadays than they were - but objectively, I believe that Voat is worse than Reddit because of the above, summarised thus:

1 - Less content (i.e., not enough content creators) 2 - Less variation in its content (i.e., less subs than reddit) 3 - It doesn't get the mainstream attention Reddit does - whenever it gets on the news for anything relevant, Voat's supposed poster-boy sub will be reported as /v/fatpeoplehate, which just turns people against Voat.

CMV, please.
CMV: Voat is objectively not as good as Reddit

This argument is based on one point which if that is your primary factor really cannot be debated and that is the amount of content. Reddit is an objectively much larger site so comparing the user base and size is silly. Other factors to consider, less censorship, less leftwing politics, smaller community which has some advantage depending on your preference, more opportunity to contribute, less mainstream media contact/celebrities/marketing.

You have partially changed my view, in that I now believe that Voat is not summarily worse off than Reddit for everyone. Instead, I now believe that, for most people (i.e. the content sponges and established content creators who need a wider audience), Voat is still an inferior good compared to Reddit, but for a small minority (i.e. aspiring content creators who need a space where their voices can be heard), Voat can be superior to Reddit.

Although it is true that Voat has a better design to make use of its users - the problem still exists that Voat simply lacks the users to make use of. Reddit, although steeped with censorship, circlejerking, and SRS, still has a wider user base to draw upon than Voat has. And ultimately, it is the user base that is the greatest determinant to the quality of user-backed sites like Reddit or Voat.

My view is that, right now, from a content-sponging perspective, there would be nearly no reason to stay on Voat or start an account on Voat - because practically everything you can find on Voat could be found on Reddit.

That said, you did make a good case for the average user of Voat - it is true that the smaller community offers more chances of relevant contributions, and it is also true that Voat is currently less market / profit- oriented than Reddit is, both of which are very relevant points to the average content creator. You have challenged my view that Voat is worse than Reddit for everyone - certainly, at the very least, Voat holds more appeal than Reddit to an aspiring content creator.

And yet - despite that - I would maintain that, from the perspective of a content seeker or established content creator who needs his audience, Voat is still worse off than Reddit. If you could change even this view, I would be very grateful. Thank you.
